chunks: And by this chain of narrators, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Ibn Abi 'Umayr, from Ibn Udhayna, from Ibn Bukayr,
he said: I said to Abi 'Abd Allah (peace be upon him): [Regarding] His saying, the Most High,
what does He mean by 'when you rise for salat'? He said: «When you rise from sleep.»
I said: Does sleep invalidate wudu? So he said: «Yes, when it overcomes the hearing and one cannot hear sound.»

key_terms.الصَّلَاةِ: salat — the obligatory ritual prayer requiring prior wudu
key_terms.النَّوْمُ: sleep — one of the nawaqid (nullifiers) of wudu in Shia fiqh
key_terms.يَغْلِبُ عَلَى السَّمْعِ: overcomes the hearing — the Imam's criterion distinguishing light dozing from sleep that nullifies wudu
key_terms.يَنْقُضُ الْوُضُوءَ: invalidates wudu — the legal determination that sleep breaks ritual purity

ai.seo_question: Does sleep invalidate wudu in Shia Islam, and what is the condition according to Imam al-Sadiq in Tahdhib al-Ahkam?
ai.summary: Ibn Bukayr asks Imam al-Sadiq (AS) to interpret the Quranic command in Q 5:6 ('when you rise for salat'); the Imam clarifies this means rising from sleep, not merely intending to pray. He then issues the legal ruling that sleep invalidates wudu specifically when it is so deep that it completely overwhelms the faculty of hearing.
